---
name: reverse-engineer-intake
description: >-
  Use whenever someone pastes or names anything to reverse engineer: a website,
  EVM contract or tx, Solana program/tx/mint, Bitcoin tx, tweet, app or binary,
  or protocol name.
---
# Paste anything → reverse engineer it

A bare paste IS the request. Don't ask what to do; start. Load `rea-setup` first if `/workspace/rea-env.sh` is missing, then `source /workspace/rea-env.sh`. Tell the user in one line what you detected and that you're starting. Delegate heavy work to a background worker.

## 1. Detect
- x.com / twitter.com link → Tweet
- `0x`+40 hex → EVM contract/wallet; `0x`+64 hex → EVM tx
- base58 32–44 chars → Solana account (check `executable` and owner)
- base58 ~87–88 chars → Solana tx signature
- 64 hex or bc1/1/3 address → Bitcoin tx/address
- other URL/domain → Website
- file: `.so` (ELF machine 263/247) → Solana program; `.apk`, `.exe`, `.dll`, Mach-O/ELF, `.app`, `.asar`, `.wasm`, bytecode hex → matching REA path
- plain words → Protocol

## 2. Route
- Tweet → read with public X tools; extract links, addresses, mints, program ids, signatures, domains; route each.
- Solana tx → `getTransaction` (jsonParsed, maxSupportedTransactionVersion 0): programs, instruction decode (Anchor = first 8 bytes vs `sha256("global:<name>")[..8]`; Shank/Borsh = 1-byte tag vs IDL), inner CPIs, SOL/token deltas, logs.
- Solana program → `solana-decompile` skill; also fetch any on-chain Anchor IDL and check the upgrade authority.
- Solana mint/account → decode by owner program (SPL Token, Token-2022, Metaplex, bonding curves); report authorities and supply.
- EVM contract → `eth_getCode` to a file; `rea inspect-evm-interface code.hex hex --json`; check EIP-1967/1167 proxies; look for verified source.
- EVM tx → receipt + trace; decode calls/logs; value and token flow.
- Bitcoin → `python /workspace/btc_rea.py <txid>`: script types, witness, OP_RETURN, inscription/Runes envelopes.
- Website → REA web/JS tools (bundles, source maps, `analyze-javascript-application`, API surface); route any contracts/programs it calls.
- App/binary → `rea doctor`, `inspect-binary-layout`, `decompile <file> <symbol>` (Ghidra), Electron/JS, .NET, Android, WASM tools.
- Protocol → official docs, repos, deployed addresses; route each.
- Other chains → identify the VM; WASM to REA WASM tools; otherwise the chain's disassembler.

## 3. Rules
Read-only. Never sign, send, spend, or execute the target. Save artifacts under `/workspace/re/<date>-<slug>/` with SHA-256s.

## 4. Report
Lead with what it does in plain words. Then addresses, instructions/functions, who controls it (authorities, upgrade keys), money flow, and risks (mint/freeze, upgradable, hidden fees, drains). Label observed / inferred / unknown. Big results go in a Page; offer to rebuild the feature.

skills.description: Use when a claim depends on a deployed Solana program's bytecode.
skills.content:
---
name: solana-decompile
description: Use when a claim depends on a deployed Solana program's bytecode.
---
# Solana decompile (REA)

1. Capture: `rea analyze-solana-program --program <id> --out <dir> --json` (read-only finalized getAccountInfo; ProgramData tag 3) or a local `.so`. Record SHA-256 and slot.
2. Analyze: `rea analyze-solana-program --elf <path> --out <dir> --json`. Read sections, `elf.trailing_bytes`, `sol_*` syscalls, strings, handler candidates. Writes `solana-analysis.json` and `disassembly.txt`.
3. Name handlers: Anchor programs use 8-byte discriminators (`sha256("global:<name>")[..8]`, pass IDL names via `--names`); Shank/Borsh programs (e.g. Metaplex) dispatch on a 1-byte tag matched to IDL order. Unmatched leads stay unnamed; some are constants, not handlers.
4. Handoff: `--handoff` writes a pinned ELF, `handoff.json`, `HANDOFF.md` for Ghidra/IDA lifting.
5. Verify: run a candidate against the original in LiteSVM/Surfpool on real-tx fixtures; recovered only when differential receipts pass.
6. Receipts: `rea solana-receipts --analysis <json>` binds verdicts to the SHA-256. Track statuses lead / identity-confirmed / receipt-verified / not-dispatch.

Never execute, sign, or broadcast. An empty handler table means unknown.
